## Employee
- Name: Sagnibha Roy (no id)
- Role: Maintenance Planner, Maintenance
- Plant / unit: Raiganj  / Unit 100

## Equipment history in the knowledge graph
- none found for this profile; interview from the profile alone and ask them to name their key equipment

topics.title: Unofficial scheduling rules when resources are tight
topics.rationale: Planner likely uses unwritten heuristics to prioritize work orders over others, which are not captured in any SOP.
seed_questions: When you have 10 high-priority work orders and only two technicians, what unwritten rules do you use to decide who goes where?
Are there certain departments or assets that always get bumped? Why?

topics.title: Critical equipment lacking a documented spare-parts strategy
topics.rationale: No equipment list is in the knowledge graph; must surface which machines have no formal spares plan and what Roy does instead.
seed_questions: Which three pieces of equipment in Unit 100 would cause the longest downtime if they failed?
For those, what spare parts do you keep unofficially 'under the shelf' that aren't in the CMMS?

topics.title: Half-finished maintenance projects and their current state
topics.rationale: Projects often stall without documented status; Roy knows what is partially done and what the remaining risks are.
seed_questions: Can you list any maintenance improvement projects that were started but never fully completed?
What would be the first step someone would need to take to finish them?

topics.title: Unwritten steps for emergency shutdown maintenance
topics.rationale: Written emergency procedures often omit tacit steps like who to call first or bypasses that are commonly used.
seed_questions: Walk me through the last emergency repair you planned; what did you do that isn't in the official procedure?
Which operator or technician should be the first call when an emergency happens at 2 AM?

topics.title: Tribal knowledge: subtle signs of impending equipment failure
topics.rationale: Maintenance planners accumulate early-warning indicators (sound, vibration, smell) that are never written down.
seed_questions: Are there any pieces of equipment that 'talk' to you before they fail? What do you listen/look for?
Has there ever been a failure you predicted but nobody believed? What were the signs?

topics.title: Vendor quirks and go-to contacts
topics.rationale: Certain vendors have undocumented lead-time tricks, unreliable parts, or specific engineers who solve problems quickly.
seed_questions: Which vendors do you always call a specific person, and what's their magic?
Are there any suppliers whose part numbers don't match the catalog? How do you handle that?

topics.title: Unfunded or stalled improvement ideas worth revisiting
topics.rationale: Roy likely has a mental list of modifications or upgrades that were rejected but would yield quick wins.
seed_questions: What is one improvement idea you've pitched multiple times but never got funded?
If you had a small budget tomorrow, what would you fix first and why?

topics.title: Recurring resource bottlenecks that no planner mentions
topics.rationale: Certain shifts, trades, or tools are chronically short, and Roy works around them silently.
seed_questions: Which shift or craft skill is always the bottleneck? How do you compensate?
Are there any tools or permits that routinely delay work but nobody complains officially?

topics.title: Informal work-order closure practices
topics.rationale: Many plants close work orders with verbal sign-offs or incomplete data; this hides true reliability gaps.
seed_questions: When is it acceptable to close a work order without a full post-maintenance test?
Are there equipment that you routinely close work orders on with just an operator's 'sounds okay'?

topics.title: Chronic repeat failures with missing root causes
topics.rationale: Some assets break again and again; the documented cause is often a symptom, not the real issue.
seed_questions: Which equipment has had the same failure three or more times? What do you suspect is the real cause?
What fix was tried multiple times that never worked, and what finally did (if ever)?

topics.title: Unofficial tuning parameters and setpoints for key systems
topics.rationale: Planners often know PID loop parameters, alarm thresholds, or control settings that differ from the official spec and are kept in someone's head.
seed_questions: Are there any controllers or drives where the actual setpoints deviate from the printed numbers? Why?
If we lost all PLC parameters tomorrow, what would you tell the technician to enter that isn't in the backup?

topics.title: Successor advice: open risks and unwritten responsibilities
topics.rationale: A maintenance planner leaves behind a web of incomplete tasks, pending vendor returns, and undocumented promises.
seed_questions: What are the top three things that could blow up in your successor's face in the first month?
Is there anything you've been promising to get done but haven't yet? What's the real deadline?

topics.title: KPI reporting tricks and hidden backlog
topics.rationale: Many planners 'manage the numbers' by reclassifying work orders or aging definitions; the successor needs to know the real backlog.
seed_questions: When you report maintenance KPIs, what do you tweak to make them look better?
How many work orders are really overdue right now, versus what the system shows?

topics.title: Lubrication and routine maintenance secrets
topics.rationale: Standard procedures for greasing, oil changes, or filter replacements often omit optimal frequencies or special techniques learned from failures.
seed_questions: Is there any equipment where you deviate from the OEM lubrication schedule? Why?
What routine task does everyone think is done but actually gets skipped? How do you know?

topics.title: Incomplete documentation for a capital project
topics.rationale: Large projects often have as-built gaps, missing manuals, or unrecorded commissioning changes that Roy knows about.
seed_questions: Which recent capital project has the worst documentation? What critical details are wrong or missing?
If we had to rebuild that project's scope tomorrow, what would you make sure we capture?
